articles.title: Benjamin Netanyahu começa discurso na Assembleia Geral da ONU | G1
articles.standfirst: Líder israelense enfrenta críticas internacionais em relação às ações no território palestino.
articles.summary: Netanyahu é um dos últimos líderes a discursar durante o debate geral da 81ª sessão da Assembleia Geral; Fala ocorre em meio à guerra em Gaza e às críticas internacionais.
articles.body:
O primeiro-ministro de Israel, Benjamin Netanyahu, discursando na 81° Assembleia Geral da Organização das Nações Unidas, em Nova York. — Foto: Mike Segar / Reuters

O primeiro-ministro de Israel , Benjamin Netanyahu , acusou nesta quinta-feira (24) o prefeito de Nova York, Zohran Mamdani , de antissemitismo. A declaração foi feita durante o discurso do israelense na Assembleia Geral da Organização das Nações Unidas (ONU). Em julho, Mamdani havia ameaçado prender Netanyahu (leia mais abaixo).

O premiê israelense chamou de 'covardes morais' as delegações que deixaram o plenário em protesto contra seu discurso e acusou países ocidentais de ceder a "multidões antissemitas". O premiê também rejeitou as acusações de genocídio contra Israel na guerra em Gaza.

"Israel não cometeu genocídio. Israel impediu um genocídio", afirmou.

O líder israelense disse, em resposta à denúncia, que Israel tomou medidas para reduzir o número de vítimas civis durante a guerra. Ele citou o envio de mensagens e panfletos para alertar moradores de áreas de combate e a vacinação contra a pólio em Gaza.

O primeiro-ministro chamou de "a maior mentira do século" a acusação de genocídio contra Israel e afirmou que o Hamas usa civis como escudos humanos.

Ao se dirigir a Mamdani, o premiê afirmou que judeus "não se sentem mais seguros em Nova York" desde a eleição do prefeito. Também acusou o político de fazer "acusações falsas e repetidas" de genocídio contra Israel e disse que Mamdani tentou impedir sua presença na ONU.

"Você não pode me silenciar. Você não pode silenciar a verdade", afirmou Netanyahu.

A Justiça internacional emitiu o mandado em 2024, no contexto da investigação sobre possíveis crimes de guerra relacionados à ofensiva israelense em Gaza.

Dias depois da ameaça de prisão, Mamdani voltou atrás e reconheceu publicamente que não possui autoridade legal para executar tal prisão.

Pouco após o discurso, o prefeito de Nova York rebateu as falas de Netanyahu. Mamdani acusou o premiê israelense de repetir mentiras infundadas com o objetivo de "maquiar o genocídio contra os palestinos".

O prefeito acrescentou ainda que "nenhuma mentira" pode mudar o fato de que Netanyahu segue alvo de um mandado de prisão do Tribunal Internacional.

Zohran Mamdani, prefeito de Nova York — Foto: Brendan McDermid/Reuters

Ainda no discurso na ONU, Netanyahu relacionou as acusações contra Israel ao antissemitismo. Segundo ele, judeus passaram a ser ameaçados e atacados em diferentes cidades do mundo por causa de sua identidade.

Netanyahu também criticou líderes de países da Europa Ocidental que, segundo ele, "cederam às multidões antissemitas" e escolheram "fraqueza" e "apaziguamento".

👉Autoridades palestinas afirmam que mais de 73 mil pessoas foram mortas na ofensiva de Israel contra a Faixa de Gaza, lançada após terroristas do Hamas matarem cerca de 1.200 pessoas no sul de Israel, em outubro de 2023.

O líder israelense começou seu discurso sob vaias e com a saída de diversos delegados do plenário. Antes de iniciar a fala, Netanyahu ironizou os representantes que deixaram a sessão. Também foram aplausos de um grupo de apoiadores que estava na galeria superior.

"Se mais algum covarde moralmente quiser sair, que saia agora!", afirmou.

Em seguida, ele disse que a ofensiva israelense contra instalações nucleares do Irã teria servido para a proteção de todo o mundo. Netanyahu se referia aos ataques militares israelense de junho do ano passado.

"Israel, ao se defender, também está defendendo muitos dos países cujos delegados acabaram de deixar este plenário", afirmou Netanyahu. Segundo ele, alguns líderes estrangeiros chegaram a agradecer Israel em particular por ter destruído instalações do programa nuclear iraniano.

O primeiro-ministro disse ainda que a decisão de atacar o programa nuclear de Teerã foi difícil, mas necessária. "Se não tivéssemos feito isso, estaríamos todos mortos", declarou.

A fala ocorre durante o terceiro dia do debate geral da 81ª sessão da Assembleia Geral, em meio ao crescente isolamento diplomático de Netanyahu .

Reino Unido e França, antigos aliados de Israel, adotaram medidas contra produtos provenientes de assentamentos israelenses na Cisjordânia, enquanto o presidente francês, Emmanuel Macron , defendeu o reconhecimento do Estado palestino em seu discurso na ONU , na última segunda-feira (21).

articles.title: Novo Onix 2027 100% etanol chega ao Acre com potência, tecnologia e economia | G1
articles.standfirst: Nova geração do Chevrolet Onix desembarca na Sabenauto com motor turbo 100% etanol, câmbio automático, seis airbags e tecnologia para transformar a experiência ao volante.
articles.summary: Nova geração do Chevrolet Onix desembarca na Sabenauto com motor turbo 100% etanol, câmbio automático, seis airbags e tecnologia para transformar a experiência ao volante.
articles.body:
Novo Onix 2027 Turbo 100% Etanol. — Foto: Divulgação/Chevrolet

O mercado automotivo acreano acaba de ganhar uma novidade que promete chamar a atenção de quem busca um carro moderno, tecnológico e econômico. A Sabenauto Chevrolet recebeu o Novo Onix 2027 100% etanol, modelo que chega reunindo desempenho, conforto, segurança e tecnologia em uma configuração pensada para quem não abre mão de inovação.

O grande destaque começa sob o capô. O Novo Onix 2027 traz motor turbo 100% etanol, colocando o combustível de fonte renovável como protagonista da experiência de dirigir. A proposta une desempenho e eficiência a uma alternativa de combustível já amplamente conhecida pelos brasileiros.

Para quem valoriza conforto ao dirigir, o modelo conta com câmbio automático de seis velocidades. A transmissão proporciona mais praticidade especialmente no trânsito urbano, tornando a condução mais confortável no dia a dia.

O Novo Onix 2027 também aposta forte em tecnologia. O veículo é equipado com Chevrolet MyLink e tela LCD sensível ao toque de 8 polegadas, oferecendo uma central moderna e intuitiva para as funções de conectividade e entretenimento.

Quando o assunto é segurança, o modelo chega preparado. São seis airbags, oferecendo uma camada adicional de proteção aos ocupantes e reforçando o compromisso do veículo com uma condução mais segura.

Estacionar e realizar manobras também ficou mais fácil. A câmera de ré auxilia o motorista na visualização da área traseira do veículo, trazendo mais praticidade para as situações do cotidiano.

Outro detalhe que chama atenção é a chave com sensor de presença. O recurso agrega praticidade à rotina e deixa a experiência com o veículo ainda mais moderna, desde o momento de acesso ao carro.

Motor turbo 100% etanol, câmbio automático de seis velocidades, MyLink com tela de 8 polegadas, câmera de ré, seis airbags e chave com sensor de presença. O conjunto coloca o Novo Onix 2027 como uma opção que reúne desempenho, tecnologia, segurança e muita praticidade.

Em um momento em que consumidores estão cada vez mais atentos às alternativas de combustível e ao impacto ambiental da mobilidade, o Novo Onix 2027 chega com uma proposta diferenciada: ser movido 100% a etanol, combustível produzido a partir de fontes renováveis.

Quem está no Acre e quer conhecer de perto o novo modelo já pode procurar a Sabenauto Chevrolet. O Novo Onix 2027 chega para conquistar olhares e apresentar uma nova experiência ao volante, combinando a tradição da Chevrolet com recursos pensados para as necessidades do motorista moderno.

Para quem procura um carro que reúna potência, tecnologia, segurança, conforto e economia, vale a pena fazer um test drive e conhecer de perto. A Sabenauto Chevrolet já está pronta para apresentar o modelo aos consumidores acreanos e mostrar todos os detalhes dessa nova experiência.

Quase 500 km com um tanque; a combinação de economia e potência

O Chevrolet Onix Eco 1.0 Turbo AT 2027 chega com uma combinação que pode agradar quem busca economia sem abrir mão de desempenho. Com tanque de 44 litros e motor 1.0 turbo de três cilindros, preparado para funcionar exclusivamente com etanol, o modelo entrega 115 cv de potência e pode alcançar cerca de 400 quilômetros de autonomia no uso urbano. Na estrada, a autonomia estimada sobe para aproximadamente 488 quilômetros, graças ao consumo médio de 11,1 km/l, contra 9,1 km/l na cidade. Na prática, os números reforçam a proposta do Onix de oferecer bom rendimento tanto na rotina dos grandes centros quanto em viagens mais longas.

articles.title: Clínicas Multidisciplinares da Unimed registram mais de 54 mil atendimentos  | G1
articles.standfirst: Estrutura reúne seis especialidades em três unidades e atende pacientes com TEA e outros transtornos do neurodesenvolvimento
articles.summary: Estrutura reúne seis especialidades em três unidades e atende pacientes com TEA e outros transtornos do neurodesenvolvimento
articles.body:
Mais de 54 mil atendimentos foram realizados entre janeiro e julho de 2026 nas três Clínicas Multidisciplinares da Unimed Cuiabá. O volume revela a dimensão da estrutura criada para oferecer acompanhamento especializado a pacientes com Transtorno do Espectro Autista (TEA) e outros transtornos do neurodesenvolvimento.

Reprodução — Foto: Assessoria | Unimed Cuiabá

Um dos diferenciais do serviço está a integração de diferentes áreas em um mesmo espaço. As unidades oferecem Psicologia, Fonoaudiologia, Terapia Ocupacional, Musicoterapia, Psicomotricidade e Psicopedagogia, permitindo que os pacientes tenham acesso a diferentes profissionais de forma integrada e reduzindo a necessidade de deslocamento entre diversos locais.

“Quando assumimos a gestão, havia apenas uma clínica. Observamos uma demanda muito grande de pacientes e poucos locais ofertando os serviços necessários. Ampliamos esse atendimento com mais duas clínicas em locais estratégicos, contratamos profissionais capacitados e hoje, com sorriso no rosto, vejo que muitas crianças neurodivergentes estão recebendo o tratamento necessário”, disse o diretor-presidente da Unimed Cuiabá, Carlos Bouret.

Mais do que reunir especialidades, o modelo busca integrar os diferentes olhares sobre cada paciente. Aspectos emocionais, cognitivos, comportamentais e funcionais podem ser avaliados por profissionais de diferentes áreas, contribuindo para uma compreensão mais ampla das necessidades individuais e para a construção de estratégias terapêuticas complementares.

Para a superintendente dos Recursos Próprios da Unimed Cuiabá, Eliane Winter, a ampliação e a estruturação desse modelo de assistência representam uma resposta concreta às necessidades dos pacientes e de suas famílias.

“A consolidação das três Clínicas Multidisciplinares demonstra o compromisso da Unimed Cuiabá em estruturar uma linha de cuidado cada vez mais qualificada para os pacientes com transtornos do neurodesenvolvimento. Mais do que ampliar a capacidade de atendimento, buscamos oferecer uma assistência integrada, com equipes especializadas e atuação multiprofissional, favorecendo a continuidade do cuidado”, afirma.

Na prática, o acompanhamento é direcionado conforme as necessidades de cada paciente. A partir das avaliações realizadas pelos profissionais, as diferentes especialidades podem atuar de forma complementar, permitindo que as estratégias terapêuticas sejam ajustadas ao longo do processo.

“Nosso compromisso é garantir que cada paciente tenha acesso a um acompanhamento individualizado, com profissionais de diferentes áreas trabalhando de forma conjunta para atender às suas necessidades e contribuir para seu desenvolvimento e qualidade de vida” , destaca a gerente das Clínicas Multidisciplinares, Bruna Evangelista.

A proposta também facilita a rotina das famílias, que encontram diferentes atendimentos concentrados em um mesmo local. Além da praticidade, a atuação integrada favorece a continuidade do cuidado e permite que os profissionais tenham uma visão mais ampla da evolução de cada paciente.

Vale frisar que, o atendimento das clínicas não é exclusivo para pessoas com TEA. As unidades também recebem pacientes com outros transtornos do neurodesenvolvimento, como o Transtorno de Déficit de Atenção com Hiperatividade (TDAH), ampliando o alcance da assistência especializada oferecida pela Unimed Cuiabá.

Mais do que realizar atendimentos, os profissionais buscam, por meio de atividades lúdicas, proporcionar diversão e aprendizados que possam ser aplicados no dia a dia. Com o uso de fantasias, garrafas PET, barbantes, tintas, entre outros materiais, as atividades estimulam os sentidos e auxiliam os pacientes no desenvolvimento da comunicação, no controle das emoções e na conquista de maior independência.

Um dos pontos fundamentais do trabalho desenvolvido nas clínicas é a participação da família no processo terapêutico. De acordo com a psicóloga e responsável técnica da Clínica Porto, Priscila Aguilera, o envolvimento dos pais e dos demais familiares que convivem com a criança é essencial para o seu desenvolvimento.

“É a família que passa a maior parte do tempo com eles. As clínicas e os profissionais somos um suporte, ensinando-os a lidar com as dificuldades. Mas, no dia a dia, é a família que está ali lidando com situações como vestir a roupa, tomar banho, fazer as lições de casa e levar para a escola. Então, é de extrema importância incluí-la no processo”, destacou.

Outro fator destacado por Aguilera foi a importância do acolhimento que muitos pais necessitam. Segundo ela, eles também precisam estar mental e psicologicamente bem para conseguirem lidar com as dificuldades do dia a dia e, junto com as crianças, trilharem esse caminho.

articles.title: Saúde pede à Conitec análise de canetas emagrecedoras no SUS | G1
articles.standfirst: Pedido envolve liraglutida e semaglutida e é uma das etapas necessárias antes de uma eventual oferta na rede pública.
articles.summary: Pedido envolve semaglutida e liraglutida e é uma das etapas necessárias antes de uma eventual oferta na rede pública.
articles.body:
O Ministério da Saúde protocolou nesta quinta-feira (24) um pedido para que a Conitec avalie a incorporação ao SUS de medicamentos à base de liraglutida e semaglutida para o tratamento da obesidade.

A presença da liraglutida no pedido amplia o leque de opções em análise. Até agora, a discussão sobre uma eventual oferta dessas canetas na rede pública vinha se concentrando principalmente na semaglutida.

A avaliação da Conitec é uma das etapas necessárias antes que esses medicamentos possam ser oferecidos de forma ampla pelo SUS.

Na semana passada, o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva afirmou que esses medicamentos seriam disponibilizados pelo SUS, mas ainda faltavam etapas técnicas para que isso pudesse ocorrer .

Hoje, o SUS não oferece de forma ampla medicamentos para o tratamento da obesidade.

Há apenas um projeto-piloto, iniciado em junho em Porto Alegre (RS), que acompanha cerca de 250 pacientes com obesidade grave ou indicação de cirurgia bariátrica.

O novo pedido ocorre em um cenário diferente do observado nas análises anteriores. Segundo o ministério, a entrada de novas marcas reduziu em cerca de 70% os preços desses medicamentos em menos de um ano.

A pasta afirma que 25 canetas já têm registro no Brasil, 14 delas aprovadas em 2026.

A queda dos preços pode mudar uma das principais questões envolvidas em uma eventual oferta pelo SUS: o custo para a rede pública .

Avaliações anteriores da Conitec apontavam impacto de bilhões de reais ao longo de cinco anos , dependendo do número de pacientes incluídos e do tempo de tratamento.

O pedido apresentado agora inclui semaglutida e liraglutida, dois princípios ativos que já não têm proteção de patente, segundo o Ministério da Saúde.

Apesar disso, mesmo com uma eventual recomendação favorável da Conitec, a chegada desses medicamentos aos pacientes ainda dependerá da definição de quem poderá recebê-los, em quais condições e de onde virão os recursos para financiar o tratamento.

Dados do Ministério da Saúde apontam que a proporção de adultos com obesidade no país passou de 11,8%, em 2006 , para 25,7%, em 2024 .

articles.title: Profissionais da educação fazem paralisação de 48 horas em Petrópolis | G1
articles.standfirst: Esta é a segunda paralisação da categoria em menos de 15 dias; trabalhadores cobram reajuste salarial, aumento do vale-alimentação e correção da tabela de pagamento
articles.summary: Esta é a segunda paralisação da categoria em menos de 15 dias; trabalhadores cobram reajuste salarial, aumento do vale-alimentação e correção da tabela de pagamento
articles.body:
Profissionais da rede municipal de educação de Petrópolis , na Região Serrana do Rio, realizaram uma paralisação de 48h. Os educadores reivindicam direitos e melhorias trabalhistas.

O movimento começou na terça-feira (23) e foi acompanhada de manifestação. Esta é a segunda paralisação da categoria em menos de 15 dias.

No dia 10 de setembro, os profissionais já haviam realizado uma paralisação de 24 horas, também acompanhada de um ato no Centro da cidade.

Esta é a segunda paralisação da categoria em menos de 15 dias. — Foto: Patrick Guimarães

De acordo com o sindicato, a nova paralisação já havia sido anunciada caso não houvesse acordo entre a categoria e a Prefeitura.

Entre as principais reivindicações estão o reajuste salarial, o aumento do vale-alimentação e a correção da tabela de pagamento de algumas funções. A entidade afirma que alguns desses valores estão abaixo do piso nacional.

“Nós não podemos aceitar isso. Prefeito querendo pagar em janeiro de 2027 um reajuste que já está atrasado. Além disso, há profissionais que recebem abaixo do piso nacional, o que é inadmissível”, afirmou Rose Silveira, representante do Sindicato Estadual dos Profissionais da Educação.

Os trabalhadores também reivindicam melhores condições de trabalho nas unidades da rede municipal, incluindo melhorias na alimentação oferecida aos alunos e aos profissionais das escolas.

Na terça-feira (23), o ato foi realizado em frente à Secretaria Municipal de Educação e à Câmara de Vereadores. Nesta quarta-feira (24), a concentração ocorreu na Praça Dom Pedro II, no Centro. Em seguida, os profissionais fizeram uma passeata pelas ruas da região e encerraram o protesto em frente à Prefeitura.

Em nota, a Prefeitura de Petrópolis informou que recebeu com surpresa a decisão da categoria de manter o estado de greve e realizar uma nova paralisação.

Segundo o município, durante uma reunião realizada no início desta semana foram apresentadas propostas para atender às reivindicações dos profissionais da educação. A administração municipal destacou ainda que segue aberta ao diálogo com os servidores.

articles.title: The Top 5 Things Flight Attendants Wish Plane Passengers Knew Before Getting on Their Next Flight
articles.summary: They don’t make the rules.
articles.body:
Flight attendants enforce airline policies and aviation regulations but rarely create the rules passengers find frustrating.

Crew members assess travelers during boarding to identify people who may be able to help during an emergency.

Most flight attendant training focuses on safety, while only a small portion covers onboard service.

When I fly , I bring a backpack for my laptop and a small suitcase. I'll sometimes tuck a fanny pack or handbag inside the backpack, since pulling it out before boarding would technically make it a third bag. Usually, I remember to keep it tucked away until I'm on the plane. Once, I didn't.

"You have three bags," a gate agent pointed out as I approached the plane. I knew the drill and stuffed my tiny crossbody into my backpack while the passengers behind me waited. One lady sighed and tapped her toes until I got situated. When I reached my seat, the flight attendant noticed that I looked a little flustered and asked if I was having a tough day. I told her about my three-bag offense. "I've always thought that rule was dumb," she said. "But I don't make the rules."

Flight attendants and other crew members enforce plenty of rules they didn't create, but that's just one of the many things passengers misunderstand about their jobs.

Travel + Leisure recently asked flight attendants what they wish more travelers knew about everything that happens before, during, and after a flight. Here's what they had to say.

Although some elements of air travel can be frustrating, most of what bugs us as passengers isn't within a flight attendant's control. Maria P., a 12-year Lufthansa veteran who goes by @realnomadgirl on Instagram , wishes passengers understood that flight attendants usually aren't the ones making the rules they enforce—like ensuring your seat is in the upright position at takeoff and landing.

"Some rules come from the airline while others are based on aviation regulations," she says. Depending on where they're operating, those regulations can come from authorities such as the Federal Aviation Administration in the U.S. or the European Union Aviation Safety Agency in Europe.

Sil, a flight attendant who has flown with the same U.S.-based airline for almost 19 years and shares travel tips on her Instagram channel, Winging It With Sil , says even rules that seem silly have a reason. "If there's a lightbulb out on a flight attendant call button, that can delay a flight. Maybe that bulb was out because of some bigger electrical problem," she explains.

She adds that the FAA is very strict—and for good reason. "The rules are written in blood. Every rule is in place because someone has been hurt."

Flight Attendants Do More Than Serve Drinks

If you pay attention to announcements from the cockpit, you're probably familiar with a line about the flight attendants being on board primarily for your safety. That's true. "We're not just waitresses in the sky," says Sil. "What the pilot says in the announcement isn't just a cliché or something that the pilot says; we truly are in-flight safety experts." She adds that only about a day and a half of her six-week training was dedicated to service. "Everything else is dedicated to how to take care of people in case of an emergency," she says.

Delays Usually Aren't Because the Crew Was Late

"Sometimes, passengers don't realize how far out of our control delays are," Sil says, explaining that most or mechanical issues. Additionally, she points out that passengers sometimes assume a delayed flight means the crew is late getting to the gate. But that's not necessarily the case. "The airlines are so strict about us showing up at the gate on time," she says. "If a flight is late because the flight attendant isn't at the gate, it's because they're on a flight coming in and that flight is late." She adds that airlines can pull a flight attendant from reserve when a crew member is delayed, but plenty of logistics are still involved.

When flight attendants greet you as you board, they're not just exchanging pleasantries. They're also watching for who can help in an emergency. "Flight attendants are trained to know who they're going to ask for help based on demeanor, conversation, or other factors that give us a clue that they're a steady person to call upon in case of emergency," says former flight attendant and travel expert Bobby Laurie .

Laurie says flight attendants notice how passengers respond when they're greeted, whether they make eye contact with the crew, and whether they appear engaged during the safety demonstration. "How quickly do they respond when you say hello? Do they ignore you? Are they wearing headphones during the safety video?" he says. "Those are all things flight attendants notice."

The Overhead Bin Above Your Seat Isn't the Only Bin You Can Use

Maria also wishes more passengers knew they can , regardless of where they're sitting. She says she'll sometimes see passengers holding their backpacks and looking disappointed when the space directly above their seat is full, even though other bins are still available. Of course, some premium-cabin sections have designated bin space, but in general, you can use any bin you'd like.

They Don't Always Know the Plane's Exact Location

Christa Treat , a Seattle-based flight attendant who has been flying for 18 years, regularly gets questions about the landscape outside the airplane window. But passengers sometimes forget that flight attendants aren't necessarily tracking the aircraft's location.

"I can't tell you how many people have pointed at the mountain range outside their window and asked me, 'What's the name of those mountains?'" she says. "I am usually not going to know where we are when we're in the air or the name of those mountains."

articles.body: Saudi Arabia issued an emergency alert for Mecca on Thursday amid an escalation in attacks by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis, warning of potential danger in the holy city for the first time during the latest flare-up.The alert was later lifted, with Saudi Civil Defence saying the danger had passed and urging residents to follow safety instructions and avoid gathering or filming. Mecca is home to Islam's holiest site, the Grand Mosque.Saudi Arabia's Saudi-led coalition in Yemen also said it had intercepted six ballistic missiles fired by the Houthis at areas including Taif and Yanbu. Houthi forces have been pushing against the Riyadh-backed government, while government forces earlier repelled overnight attacks on the Taiz-Aden road, a key supply route to the southern port city of Aden.The fighting is the latest episode in Yemen's 12-year civil war, which had largely been frozen since a 2022 truce. articles.title: SC flags ‘false’ POCSO cases in marital disputes, bars immediate arrest of accused parent
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday laid down safeguards against the immediate arrest of a parent or family member accused under the POCSO Act when
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday laid down safeguards against the immediate arrest of a parent or family member accused under the POCSO Act when the alleged offence involves a child living under the same roof and there is a matrimonial dispute between the child's parents.A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K V Viswanathan, flagging a rise in fakecases, said police should not act in haste in such cases and directed that, as a general rule, an expert in child and adolescent psychiatry or clinical psychology should evaluate the child before authorities decide whether there is sufficient reason to arrest the accused.The court said the safeguards were necessary in cases where allegations may be influenced by a strained relationship between the parents. It stressed that the measures do not dilute the seriousness of offences under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, but are intended to ensure that the power of arrest is exercised after considering all relevant circumstances.The court said immediate arrest should not take place when two conditions are present: a POCSO offence is alleged against a parent or family member living with the child, and a matrimonial dispute exists between the child's parents, whether or not the dispute is pending before a court.The police officer receiving the complaint must verify whether such a matrimonial dispute exists, the court said. "When the above-stated threshold conditions are met, post the registration of an FIR, we are of the considered opinion that the investigating officer should not act in haste or take coercive actions in the form of arrest immediately," the bench added, as quoted by PTI.The verdict came in a matrimonial dispute involving an estranged Bengaluru couple. The wife had alleged that the child was sexually assaulted. The case was investigated by the CBI, which found the allegation to be false. The Supreme Court restored custody of the child to the father, taking into account the welfare of the minor.The court also directed the investigating officer or the Special Juvenile Police Unit to seek the services of an expert in child and adolescent psychiatry or clinical psychology, in consultation with the District Child Protection Unit or, where one is unavailable, the District Legal Services Authority, adding that the expert's evaluation must be conducted independently and without influence from either the parent or investigating authorities.After receiving the evaluation, investigators must consider the expert's opinion along with other evidence and circumstances before deciding whether there is "reason to believe" that the accused committed the offence and whether an arrest is warranted. The court said an exception could be made in cases where the material available is "palpable", allowing the investigating officer to dispense with an expert evaluation, but reasons for doing so must be recorded in writing.The bench also stressed that arrest is not automatically required merely because an offence is cognisable. The court said an arrest can cause "irreparable harm" to an accused parent or family member, particularly where the allegation later turns out to be unfounded.The Supreme Court also raised concerns about the consequences of allegations on children and their relationship with the accused parent."The trauma that a child is put through in the process and the accusation can damage the very fabric of the parent-child relationship," the bench said, adding that such a wound could leave an "indelible scar" on both the child and parent.The court also flagged what it described as an increase in false allegations in matrimonial disputes."What is alarming is that this tendency of making false accusations is on the rise," it said.The bench cautioned against parents being influenced by advisers during matrimonial disputes, saying that some may be driven by a "win at any cost" approach.At the same time, the court said the safeguards were not a finding that allegations made in such circumstances are false. Investigating authorities must examine the allegations along with the surrounding circumstances and other evidence.For complaints filed directly before a special court, the Supreme Court said an order taking cognisance and summoning an accused must demonstrate application of mind. The special court should also involve an expert in child and adolescent psychiatry or clinical psychology to evaluate the child and submit a report.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Gaza’s recovery needs reach $71.5bn amid ‘most severe economic crisis’: UN
articles.summary: UN trade body report says consequences of Israeli occupation have ‘skyrocketed’ with 90% unemployed in Gaza.
articles.body:
Gaza’s recovery and reconstruction needs have reached an estimated $71.5bn and are likely to increase, according to the latest United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD) report.

Gaza’s economy has experienced the world’s “most severe crisis on record”, said the report presented at UNCTAD’s 73rd session on Thursday.

It said that 59 years of Israeli occupation have “imposed structural constraints that have systemically stunted the Palestinian economy”, undermining productivity, deepening poverty and forcing dependence on aid.

But since Israel launched its genocidal war in October 2023, the consequences of the occupation have “skyrocketed”.

Israel’s “intense” military operations have damaged or destroyed 92 percent of economic establishments across Gaza since the war began. Unemployment has surged, with over 90 percent of Gaza’s working-age population unemployed, the report said.

At the same time, hundreds of thousands of jobs have been lost across the Occupied Palestinian Territories, erasing $2.8bn in cumulative labour income, it added.

Gaza’s GDP per capita last year was $212 ($0.58 a day) – an 83 percent decrease since 2022, it said.

A separate assessment by the World Bank, EU and UN put Gaza’s physical infrastructure damage at $35.2bn and economic and social losses at $22.7bn as of early 2026, with the $71.5bn reconstruction estimate “likely to increase”, according to UNCTAD.

Housing accounts for the largest share of Gaza’s damage and reconstruction needs, while more than half of hospitals and clinics remain non-functional and less than 1.5 percent of cropland remains accessible and undamaged.

The report said the damage requires “large-scale international financial and technical assistance” to rebuild agriculture, industry, construction, energy and technology, and called for transferring withheld Palestinian revenues, safeguarding the banking system and aligning reconstruction support with the documented scale of damage as immediate priorities.

Israel withholds funds as West Bank in crisis

Israel withheld clearance revenue transfers – collected on the Palestinian Government’s behalf under the Paris Protocol, an arrangement the report notes is “over 27 years past its expiry date” – from May 2025 through mid-2026.

Cumulative deductions and withheld revenues between 2019 and March 2026 exceeded $3.67bn, equivalent to 83 percent of total Palestinian net revenue in 2025.

With the Palestinian Authority’s 2025 budget deficit reaching 13 percent of GDP, the fiscal pressure is straining essential services: health-related arrears hit $1.1bn by late 2025, threatening hospitals and pharmaceutical suppliers, while resource shortages forced West Bank schools to limit in-person instruction to three days a week.

Public debt has reached $4.8bn, with banking-sector exposure to the public sector at $5.3bn, or 42 percent of all bank lending.

“Systemic collapse is no longer a theoretical possibility,” the report warned.

“Banks may soon be unable to sustain essential trade flows, including fuel, water and medicine, and stabilising the financial system and developing a sustainable cross-border payments framework is an urgent priority.”

Separately, the report documents reduced Palestinian access to land amid settlement expansion, with 38 communities emptied since 2023 and first-quarter 2026 displacement already exceeding all of last year.

articles.title: Ministers reject dog ownership licence scheme
articles.summary: A taskforce had suggested new legal requirements could help promote dog control and reduce attacks.
articles.body:
Pet owners will not have to pay a fee to own a dog, after the government ruled out introducing a licensing scheme.

In a report, published on Thursday, a panel of animal experts suggested the government should consider new legal requirements for dog owners.

The panel did not reach an agreement on which rules should be adopted but the taskforce said any new laws should aim to promote better dog control, reduce the risk of dog attacks and avoid placing an "undue burden" on owners.

A spokesperson for the environment department said: "This is a welcome report and ministers are considering the taskforce's recommendations, however we will not be introducing a new dog licensing scheme."

The Dog Control Coalition - which includes the RSPCA, Battersea Dogs & Cats Home and the Royal Kennel Club - said it supported the recommendations in the report and that it was "vital" for the government to take action "as a matter of urgency".

A spokesperson for the coalition said: "Dog bite incidents continue to have serious consequences for people and dogs, and the time that has passed since the publication of The Middlesex Report, in 2021, makes it imperative that we now see progress."

The report made 20 recommendations including calling for councils to provide a service to tackle low-level dog control issues, improved recording of dog bite wounds and legal requirements for dog walkers.

Dog attacks are still rising - even after the XL bully ban

What are the rules for having an XL bully dog?

Dog licences explored to tackle ownership issues

The Responsible Dog Ownership Taskforce was established by the government in 2022, following a series of high-profile dog attacks.

The taskforce's report noted that since 2011 the dog population in the UK had grown by 35%, while hospital admissions relating to dog bites in England had risen by 77%.

It said pet ownership had spiked during the Covid pandemic at a time when it was harder to access support services.

"This led to less experienced owners struggling to access services and finding it harder to get help," the report said.

Until 1987, dog owners in England, Wales and Scotland had to pay an annual fee to get an ownership licence.

The scheme was scrapped on the grounds that the amount of money it raised was outweighed by the operating costs.

Dog owners in Northern Ireland still have to buy a licence of £12.50, or £5 if the owner receives an income-related benefit.

In France, owners of the most dangerous dogs have to get special permits which can involve passing a training course and putting the dog through a behavioural assessment.

Switzerland previously required potential dog owners to complete a knowledge test, followed by a practical, but this condition has been scrapped.

The report said that most members of the taskforce backed introducing legal requirements for dog owners but "further consideration would be needed regarding the form that this should take".

"Any legal requirement would need careful consideration of its objective and not appear as a tax on already responsible dog owners.

"Reintroducing a universal dog licence may amount to another database of responsible owners or an administrative exercise with little public safety benefit or opportunity to promote responsible dog ownership."

It said options could include focusing a scheme on high-risk dogs, introducing background checks on owners and requiring potential owners to pass a knowledge test.

The Dogs Trust and the RSPCA have commissioned research into the costs and benefits of different systems and their conclusions are due to be published later this year.

In a ministerial foreword to the report, environment minister Baroness Hayman of Ullock said: "In recent years, we have seen a concerning rise in dog attacks, alongside changes in patterns of dog ownership."

She said the taskforce's report was an "important and timely contribution", adding: "As ministers, we are carefully considering the recommendations alongside the wider programme of work already under way."

articles.title: Rapper Macklemore announces 'Free Palestine' tour after Ed Sheeran fallout
articles.summary: Proceeds from the tour, which begins in Dublin next month, will go to organisations supporting Palestinians, he says.
articles.body:
Rapper Macklemore is launching a "Free Palestine" tour, days after being dropped from Ed Sheeran's Loop Tour following pro-Palestinian comments he made onstage earlier this month.

"So, as you all know, my schedule freed up a bit," he said upon announcing the tour on Thursday.

The American artist - whose real name is Benjamin Haggerty - said proceeds from the tour, which launches in Dublin next month, will go to organisations supporting Palestinians.

Macklemore's onstage comments and subsequent removal from the tour led Sheeran's support acts to drop out, while the British singer stressed that the decision to drop the rapper was made by his promoter, not by himself.

Everything we know about the Ed Sheeran and Macklemore controversy

In a statement on Thursday, the rapper said that the last couple of weeks had shown him there had been "a collective awakening around Palestinian liberation, the power of billionaires that try to censor that call, and what we expect from artists right now".

"What happened to me is bigger than one artist or one stage," he said. "When the billionaire class can decide which voices are allowed on stage and which ones are too dangerous to hear, everyone should be paying attention."

Macklemore said he had spent the last week contacting artists who had used their platforms to stand in solidarity with the Palestinian people, regardless of the consequences.

Due to how quickly the tour came together, several details were still being worked out, he added: "But this is a moment of momentum, and there is work to be done."

Macklemore's new tour will begin in Dublin on 26 October followed by Paris on 29 October and London on 30 October.

US dates will also be added, he said, with additional tickets going on sale next week.

While performing as the opening act for Sheeran at a concert in early September in New Jersey, Macklemore said: "A big part of the reason why I wanted to do this tour in the first place is so that I could stand up in stadiums like this and say two words that are very, very dear to my heart: Free Palestine."

The Thrift Shop rapper then performed a song dedicated to pro-Palestinian protesters at Columbia University.

After he was taken off the tour on 14 September, Macklemore accused stadium owners of rallying together to push him out. He was also accused by billionaire stadium owner Robert Kraft of hate speech and antisemitic rhetoric surrounding Israel and Gaza.

Sheeran early on said that the decision to drop Macklemore from his tour was made by concert promoter Messina Touring Group.

His early remarks led to all of his support acts to drop out of the tour in solidarity, and fans to express frustration. Ticket prices for the tour plummeted as well.

Sheeran addressed the controversy head-on during the start of his set in Philadelphia last week.

He said he had made "mistakes" handling the fallout, apologising to fans and taking a stand on the Israel-Gaza conflict, which he said was "a humanitarian issue".

He described the 7 October 2023 Hamas-led attacks as "horrific", and also called the situation in Gaza "unjustifiable and disproportionate".

articles.title: 'It has broken us as a family,' mother of poison seller victim tells hearing
articles.summary: Tanya Whitaker broke down before she spoke of how her son Samuel's death had devastated her family.
articles.body:
The mother of a British victim of poison seller Kenneth Law has said his death and the way that he died had "destroyed" their family.

Tanya Whitaker broke down at the start of her video statement about the death of her son, Samuel, shown on the second day of a four-day sentencing hearing of Law in Ontario, saying: "He barely had a chance."

The University of Warwick student was found collapsed outside his halls after taking poison sold by Law, who has admitted 14 counts of aiding suicide in Canada. British authorities have confirmed 79 UK victims also died after using his products.

Debbie Cornish echoed Whitaker's sentiments, telling the hearing that her family was "still fighting" to stay together years on from her daughter Danielle's death.

A plea deal with Canadian authorities means Law will not face charges in the UK or over any British deaths, but impact statements from their families are being read this week.

"The enormity of losing a child is catastrophic," Whitaker told a Canadian court on Thursday. "Samuel was just 19 when he was handed the tools that ended his precious life."

She continued: "It has broken me completely and utterly. It has broken us as a family and me as a mother.

"Our son died alone at university 100 miles away from his family. We will never be able to forgive ourselves for this happening."

Whitaker said Samuel had been the only biological son of her husband, Paul.

"He is a shell of himself today. Broken and devastated beyond repair," she added.

Cornish, the mother of British victim Danielle, spoke of her anguish in a written statement, in which she referred to Law only by the initials KL.

"Words on paper can't even begin to describe the painful loss of our amazing daughter," she said.

"Nothing will be the same ever again as we are part of a surreal nightmare.

"Nearly four years on, we are still fighting to keep our family together... not to mention the constant thoughts of how she may have died.

"KL has changed the life of many many families all across the world as well as ours. We are living a constant nightmare."

Authorities say Law, a former chef, sold about 1,200 packages of toxic substances to recipients from 40 different countries he met in online suicide forums. Roughly a quarter of the packages were sent to the UK.

He was arrested in May 2023, following a complex investigation by at least 11 law-enforcement agencies that involved investigators from around a dozen countries, including the UK, Italy and the US.

The court also heard a statement from Faith George, the mother of Faith Ike-Elechi, who referred to her daughter by the nickname Chimma.

She found her daughter helpless on the floor after she had taken the poison, and said her last works "echo in my mind every day".

She said if she were able to speak to her daughter again she would tell her she had never stopped being proud of her.

Maurice Dunham, father of British victim Michael Dunham, said the last time he saw his son alive was on a family holiday to Croatia that Michael had left early to return home.

"The last conversation I had with him was an argument," he said in a written statement.

Maurice returned home days later and discovered Michael was dead.

"The feeling I had was like an electric shock going through me," he wrote. "I blamed myself for not stopping Michael from leaving the hotel room.

"I planned to take my own life. I didn't care if I lived or died."

Later, the court heard the words of the mother of Yeanu Mistry, who said hearing he had died was "the news every parent fears".

And Maureen Cooper, the mother of poison victim Gary Cooper, called the pain of losing her son "unbearable".

"A death such as this is the thing of nightmares," her written statement said.

Aimee Louise Elif Walton, from Southampton, died in "the company of a stranger [she] met online", her sister told the court.

Adele Zeynep Walton said in a video played at the hearing that someone from a suicide forum had flown from the US and stayed with her in a hotel room for the 11 days leading up to her death.

"She died in a strange place, in a strange city, in the company of a stranger," her sister said.

"You only need to listen to the recording of the emergency call to know how much she suffered during the last moments of her life."

On Wednesday, the court heard from a British survivor who was given an antidote that saved her after taking poison from Law.

Elisabeth Belien told the court: "I feel guilty for surviving. Although I survived, it has also impacted my loved ones. I feel like my vulnerability was exploited. I still feel a lot of shame about what happened."

articles.title: ​In 1997, John Oates built a five-bedroom log home on his 4.3-acre Colorado ranch after starting with largely undeveloped land; 28 years later, the longtime retreat sold for $6.9 million
articles.summary: When John Oates first laid eyes on the property in Woody Creek, Colorado, just outside Aspen, it wasn't much to look at.
articles.body: When John Oates first laid eyes on the property in Woody Creek, Colorado, just outside Aspen, it wasn't much to look at. The musician had another house in mind, an Aspen townhouse that sat right downtown. But his girlfriend at the time, and soon-to-be wife, Aimee, saw something different. “She grew up on a farm in Illinois, a farm girl from the Midwest, and when she saw the house in town she liked it and all, but she said, ‘Boy, I wish we could have chickens.’ I knew right then we needed some land,” Oates told The Land Report earlier.They started looking for properties with the help of his friend, a realtor in town. One of the properties was in Woody Creek. "It was literally raw land with two dilapidated cabins. Basically, a barn and a cabin," he told the outlet. The couple thought it felt right and bought it. By 1997, Oates and his wife had transformed the land into what became known as Little Woody Creek Ranch. After owning it for nearly three decades, the couple sold the Aspen ranch for $6.9 million, Realtor.com reported.The Little Woody Creek Ranch they builtAfter purchasing the 4.3-acre property in 1994, the couple started building their dream abode. For nearly three decades, the Oates family used the ranch as their Colorado escape. Between their primary home in Nashville and this sprawling mountain refuge, they split their time between the two, returning to Colorado for holidays and getaways.The rock 'n' roll legend called Woody Creek the ‘bohemian suburb of Aspen’. Why? Because he felt right at home. In Manhattan, he lived in Greenwich Village, which is flooded with artists, musicians, actors and all types of creative people. This Colorado ranch had the same vibe. “I felt right at home in Woody Creek from the very beginning. Don Henley lived down the road. Don Johnson lived not far from him. Jimmy Ibbotson from The Nitty Gritty Dirt Band lived up the road from us; still does. And Hunter Thompson lived across the street. My closest neighbour was Bob Beattie, the legendary ski coach, who we shared a lane with. It was this really great community of well-known but down-home people,” he told the outlet.The accessibility also attracted the Oates family. It’s about eight miles from downtown Aspen. “The good news is you don’t have to take Highway 82, which is the main highway. That can get very crowded in-season. McLain Flats Road parallels Highway 82, and you can literally just drive in and out of town with no traffic.”Listing the propertyIn 2017, the couple listed the property for $6 million. The couple decided to list it after they realised that they were spending less time in Colorado. They were spending more months in Nashville. The ranch no longer needed to sustain horses or the lifestyle it had supported for decades. So they decided to list it. "Longtime Woody Creek residents, John and Aimee Oates have decided to relocate to downtown Aspen and put their 35-year home on the market," the description listed by Scott Davidson of Christie's International Real Estate read.For months, the ranch didn’t find a prospective buyer. It sat on the market for months, even after price cuts. By the end of 2018, they pulled it from the market. Eight years would pass before they tried again.In June 2024, the ranch went back on the market at $7.5 million. In less than two months, a buyer came, and the sale closed at $6.9 million. Records confirm that the sale closed on July 30. This marks the end of an era for the Oates family at their Creek ranch.What the $6.9 million boughtThe Little Woody Creek Ranch is a ‘perfect example of a gentleman’s ranch’, according to the listing. But the property also has several features suited to a working ranch. Set against the breathtaking mountain views, the 4.3-acre property is centred around a five-bedroom, 4.5-bathroom log home with spacious interiors. The house comes with high ceilings and a large stone fireplace, perfect for the winter. The living space flows into the open-plan kitchen and dining area, where one can host multiple guests.The master suite comes with its own fireplace, a marble vanity with dual sinks and a separate soaking tub. There's a separate caretaker unit with its own kitchen and bathroom. The game room displays Oates' gold and platinum records, a perk for music enthusiasts. It also has a two-car garage and a home gym.Beyond the main structure, there is a horse stable, equipment shed and outbuildings. The ranch also has an automated irrigation system and a fire suppression system that runs off an 18,000-gallon tank buried underground. According to the listing, there are two wells: one for domestic use and the other for agricultural use.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Trump admin to ask Supreme Court to revive 3rd-country deportations after court blocks policy
articles.summary: The Trump administration plans to appeal to the Supreme Court to reinstate its policy on third-country deportations after a federal appeals court deemed it unlawful. This move follows a class-action lawsuit regarding migrants' rights and safety concerns associated with such deportations.
articles.body: The Trump administration will ask the US Supreme Court to revive its policy of deporting migrants to countries other than their own after a federal appeals court blocked the practice.US Attorney General Todd Blanche said on Thursday that the Department of Justice would seek relief from the Supreme Court, arguing that the administration should be allowed to continue third-country removals.The move follows a ruling by a three-judge panel of the US Court of Appeals for the First Circuit in Boston that upheld a lower court decision finding the Department of Homeland Security's policy unlawful. The case is part of a class-action lawsuit brought by migrants facing deportation.The legal dispute centres on whether migrants must be allowed to raise safety concerns before being removed to a country with which they have no connection. The appeals court ruling put the administration's third-country deportation policy on hold.Blanche criticised the appeals court decision in a post on X, saying it had blocked the government from carrying out third-country removals. He said the administration would seek the Supreme Court's intervention, noting that the justices had previously granted a stay in the same case.The administration has reached agreements with other countries that have enabled more than 25,000 migrants to be deported to at least 29 countries, according to Third Country Deportation Watch, a project by Refugees International and Human Rights First. Mexico has been the destination in many cases, while others have been sent to countries across Latin America, Central Asia, the Caribbean and Africa.Some deportees have been sent to countries facing serious security or humanitarian problems, including the Central African Republic and South Sudan.The DHS has defended the policy. James Percival, the agency's general counsel, rejected criticism that the deportations were cruel, arguing that allowing migrants who cannot be returned to their home countries to remain in US communities posed its own risks.You use AI every day. articles.title: Bodies of 5th grade teacher and 10-year-old student recovered from water following incident during Iowa field trip
articles.summary: The bodies of a 5th-grade student and teacher were recovered from the water at Lake MacBride State Park in Iowa following an incident during a field trip.
articles.body: The bodies of a 5th-grade student and teacher were recovered from the water at Lake MacBride State Park in Iowa following an incident during a field trip. The Johnson County Sheriff’s Office was called to the park Tuesday afternoon for reports of people in the water near Coralville Reservoir, a news release states. The body of Hannah Jorgensen, 24, of Tiffin, was pulled from the water around 12:43 p.m., and a search was launched for a missing 10-year-old boy. The child, Ahmed Osman, of Iowa City, was found dead Wednesday, authorities said in an update. Fifth-grade students from Borlaug Elementary School were on a “School of the Wild Field Trip,” NBC affiliate KWWL of Waterloo, Iowa, reported. Iowa City Community School District confirmed the deaths in a Facebook post on Thursday. “Our hearts are shattered by the loss of two beloved members of our Borlaug Elementary family, fifth-grade teacher Hannah Jorgensen and fifth-grade student Ahmed Osman. There are simply no words that can adequately express the depth of this loss,” the district said. “Hannah and Ahmed were so much more than members of our school community. They were a teacher and student, a colleague and classmate, a friend, and most importantly, deeply loved members of their families.” The district said “their absence will be felt in the classrooms and hallways of Borlaug, in the lives of those who loved them, and throughout our entire school district community.” “We will remember Hannah. We will remember Ahmed. And we will carry their memory with us,” the statement read. Norman Borlaug Elementary School thanked the community for its support. “Our building is hurting right now, and so are our hearts. But knowing that you are all here for us, standing beside us, checking in, and, lifting us up. It means more than we can put into words,” the school said. The sheriff’s office said the incident remains under investigation.

articles.title: Trump's war on press runs into judicial hurdle; court order White House to let journos back in
articles.summary: TOI correspondent from Washington: In a surreal drama that was played out on the sidelines of Chinese President Xi Jinping visit – covered by a phalanx of
articles.body: TOI correspondent from Washington: In a surreal drama that was played out on the sidelines of Chinese President Xi Jinping visit – covered by a phalanx of not-so-free press from China – the Trump administration on Thursday was forced to allow reporters from CNN, MS NOW and Politico into the White House after initially defying a court order asking it to revoke President Trump’s ban on them.US District Judge Timothy Kelly -- a Trump appointee -- ruled Thursday morning that the three organizations' access should be immediately restored for 14 days while their lawsuit against the White House proceeds. In doing so, the judge noted an inconvenient fact for the President: when Trump announced the ban, he himself had emphasized the supposedly false and negative nature of the outlets' coverage, rather than national security issues the administration later invoked to make its case for the ban.And so ended, for the moment, one of the more bizarre mornings in the modern history of the White House press corps: the president banned the reporters, the reporters sued, a judge ordered them back, the White House kept them out anyway, the reporters went back to court -- and then the reporters were let in. For now.The sequence began last Friday when Trump announced that CNN, MS NOW and Politico would no longer have access to the White House, accusing them of producing “FAKE NEWS” and saying their reporting was false and negative. The three organizations promptly sued, arguing that the ban violated their First Amendment and Fifth Amendment rights.The dispute has already produced another extraordinary development: major television networks had suspended their normal White House video pool in solidarity with the excluded outlets. ABC, CBS, CNN, NBC, and even Fox News -- a pro-Trump echo chamber -- jointly argued that the public has a right to independent information about its government and access should not depend on whether a news organization pleases the president.Trump, naturally, was not impressed with the press ganging up -- supported by the judiciary for now. Between preparing to welcome President Xi, he raged about reporters, calling them sleazebags, lunatics, sick, demented, treasonous etc and even unloaded on the judge he himself had appointed, calling him “totally disloyal.” At one point, he even posted an AI-generated image depicting the banned news organizations as trash bags outside the White House and another reporter as a homeless hobo.The legal fight is not over. Judge Kelly's order lasts 14 days while the underlying case proceeds, and the administration can continue to argue that it has authority to control access to the White House complex. The news organizations maintain that they were singled out because of their coverage (by Trump’s own admission) and were denied the notice and opportunity to challenge the decision required by due process.It is, in other words, back to business in Washington -- where the president wants the last word, the press wants the next story, and the courts occasionally insist on having both.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 1888, George Vanderbilt began building a vast North Carolina estate; 26 years later, his widow sold 86,700 acres for $433,500, helping create the core of Pisgah National Forest in 1916
articles.summary: A major property deal that began more than a century ago with a grieving widow turned a huge private wilderness in North Carolina into one of the most
articles.body: A major property deal that began more than a century ago with a grieving widow turned a huge private wilderness in North Carolina into one of the most important public conservation achievements in American history. In May 1914, Edith Vanderbilt agreed to sell 86,700 acres of valuable mountain forest from the private Biltmore Estate to the United States federal government for $433,500. The deal was made at $5.00 per acre and moved the huge forest area into public ownership. The land later became the foundation of Pisgah National Forest, which was formally established in 1916. The sale carried out the conservation plan of her late husband, George Washington Vanderbilt. He began buying worn-out farmland and mountain slopes near Asheville, North Carolina, in 1888. Over 26 years, he collected more than 125,000 acres to build a self-sufficient mountain retreat centered around the 250-room Biltmore House.Building a cradle of forestryWhen George Vanderbilt first bought land in Western North Carolina, years of uncontrolled logging and burning had badly damaged local watersheds and forests. To restore the land, Vanderbilt hired famous landscape architect Frederick Law Olmsted and young forestry expert Gifford Pinchot, who later became the first chief of the United States Forest Service. Under their direction, the Biltmore property became a testing ground for scientific forest management and soil restoration across the American South. In 1898, German forester Carl A. Schenck founded the Biltmore Forest School on the estate. It became the first school of professional forestry in North America. After George Vanderbilt unexpectedly died in March 1914 from complications following surgery, keeping the huge private property became a major financial burden for his widow. Edith Vanderbilt chose to follow her husband's wish to preserve the mountain wilderness instead of selling the land to commercial timber companies. According to historical records documented by the Forest History Society, Edith wrote directly to United States Secretary of Agriculture David F. Houston on 1 May 1914 to formally offer the land to the federal government. In her letter, she explained that she wanted the land protected for the public. She wrote: "I wish to sell this tract of land to the Government at a price significantly below its commercial value in order that my husband's plan for the protection of these mountain forests may be permanently realized."Anchoring public land conservationThe purchase was made possible by the Weeks Act, a federal law passed by the United States Congress in 1911. The law allowed the federal government to buy private land in eastern states to protect the headwaters of navigable rivers and manage forest resources. The National Forest Reservation Commission, led by Secretary Houston, quickly approved the deal. Official commission records kept in the Forest History Society archives show that the government considered the $5.00-per-acre price an exceptional bargain. Private timber companies had offered much more for the right to cut down the forests. The transaction was completed in 1914. Only 10,000 acres around the main Biltmore House and its immediate grounds remained in private family ownership. On 17 October 1916, President Woodrow Wilson issued an executive proclamation creating Pisgah National Forest, with the former Vanderbilt land serving as its central area.Enduring environmental heritageThe purchase protected important headwater areas for major river systems in the region, including the French Broad River basin. Today, Pisgah National Forest covers more than 500,000 acres across the Appalachian Mountains. Millions of people visit the forest each year for hiking, scientific research, and wildlife conservation. The birthplace of American forestry is still preserved within the forest at the Cradle of Forestry in America National Historic Site. The site stands on the same grounds where Schenck's students once attended their original field lectures. By accepting a much lower price for the land, Edith Vanderbilt protected both the financial future of the remaining estate and a large area of North American wilderness for future generations. The deal remains one of the largest single land purchases made under the Weeks Act and helped set an example for protecting public land across the eastern United States.You use AI every day. articles.title: BBC upholds complaints over Victoria Beckham slur on Have I Got News For You
articles.summary: Two viewers complained to the BBC over the "gratuitously offensive" comment made during the show.
articles.body:
Complaints about the broadcast of a swear word in connection with Victoria Beckham during an episode of BBC One's Have I Got News For You have been upheld, the corporation's executive complaints unit (ECU) has ruled.

The show, from 7 November last year, hosted by comic and presenter Katherine Ryan, featured an email allegedly sent by Sir David Beckham in which the word was used.

Ryan told the show's panellists: "I don't know that we are allowed to broadcast the c-word, but you did reference Victoria Beckham earlier and we'll allow that."

Two viewers complained that this was gratuitously offensive, and the BBC said there was no justification for a comment which "presented Victoria Beckham as equivalent to a particularly offensive word".

The ECU finding has been reported to the management of BBC Content.

As a result, a version of the programme edited in light of the finding will replace the version currently on iPlayer.

The ECU statement in full said: "The relevant BBC Editorial Guidelines do not require programmes to avoid giving offence, but do require that any offence should be editorially justified.

"In the ECU's judgement, while the inclusion of the c-word in the programme derived editorial justification from David Beckham's alleged use of it and the satirical reflections this prompted, there was no such justification for a comment which presented Victoria Beckham as equivalent to a particularly offensive word."

In November , the ECU responded to complaints from viewers it said were "unhappy with the inclusion of strong language in the programme".

It said "the use of the strong language was editorially justified as the panel were discussing a current news story about Sir David Beckham and directly quoting from leaked emails in which he had used the word in question, leading to further discussion".

It added that it was "common practice" to carry a clear verbal warning at the start of post-watershed programmes with very strong language, which was what happened for this particular episode of the show.

"It is never our intention to offend our audience," the statement added.

articles.title: She Started an Allergy-Friendly Snack Brand So Her Daughter Wouldn’t Feel Left Out. Now, the Girl Scouts Are Selling Her Cookies
articles.summary: Denise Woodard started allergy-friendly cookie company, Partake, so her daughter wouldn’t feel left out. Now, she’s selling her cookies with the Girl Scouts.
articles.body: Denise Woodard remembers standing in her home kitchen in 2019, already thinking big. “We had one other employee, and I was like, ‘We’re going to make a Girl Scout cookie one day,’” she recalls. “I think she thought I had lost the plot!” But Woodard was right. As a dietitian and food-allergy parent, I know first-hand the terror of the first reaction you see. It may unfold in just seconds, but dealing with the implications can take a lifetime. You learn to make substitutes for your mealtime staples or pack homemade snacks, but it’s not long before a school event or friend’s party leaves your child empty-handed, watching the others enjoy a special treat. All allergy families know that pain of shielding their child from the world to keep them safe. How many change the world instead? Woodard and her 11-year-old daughter, Vivienne, are doing just that, with a little help from the Girl Scouts of America. When Vivienne was just 8 months old, she had a reaction to a dish at her first Thanksgiving and was soon diagnosed with food protein-induced enterocolitis syndrome (FPIES) to eggs. This kind of reaction is different from the usual food allergy; it’s delayed by at least a couple of hours, and the symptoms are largely gastrointestinal. Severe reactions can progress to shock, however, and they can’t be treated with epinephrine. As is true for many with FPIES, Vivienne also developed severe typical food allergies. Suddenly, Woodard had to figure out not just how to feed her daughter with nourishing ingredients free of eggs, nuts, corn and sesame, but also how to help her engage in regular social life — play dates and special occasions — safely. Although she worked in food product sales, Woodard says she had no idea how food allergies affect the people who have them, and their families, until the severity of Vivienne’s corn allergy shook her. “I feel embarrassed by how much I trivialized it until I was living the journey myself,” Woodard told me, “but you realize that food is such a massive part of every single event and every single thing that you do, and then you have to send your kid out into this world where things that are just so common can actually be deadly for them.” Woodard admits she felt discouraged by the list of allergens at first, and credits Vivienne’s nanny Martha with helping her kick into gear. Making a truly safe, truly delicious sweet treat without a bunch of questionable ingredients is easier said than done, but they got into the kitchen to figure things out. She also decided to leverage every dime toward making this dream a reality for everyone. She left her corporate job in 2017, and with some assistance from a professional food product developer, her retail product line was on its way. Although she initially funded her efforts by draining her 401K and even selling her engagement ring, her idea struck a chord with investors like Jay-Z’s Marcy Venture Partners, and in 2019, she became the first Black woman to raise over $1 million for a packaged food company. Much of the packaging for such product lines screams “substitute” instead of “scrumptious,” but it was important to Woodard that kids (and adults) like Vivienne feel seamlessly included. She named her company Partake because it’s her mission to let everyone take part without being set apart, and you’d never know the brand is free of the top-nine allergens if you didn’t read the fine print on the tempting label. There are multiple flavors to suit every taste, from grahams to wafers to snaps. In fact, Partake’s market research shows that about half of their customers don’t have severe food allergies. Vivienne has helped with flavor ideas a bit, but she relishes her main role as taste-tester. Her favorite? The Teeny-Tiny Crunchy Chocolate Chip. “I like how small they are, so you can just pop them in your mouth,” she says. The Teeny-Tinies might have some competition soon, though. In January of 2027, the cookie that Partake and Girl Scouts co-created will hit the website for digital orders from Girl Scouts like Vivienne herself. They’re called Sparkables, and they’ve got chocolate chips and a rainbow of colored sprinkles that will make any kid want to partake, allergies or not. “We wanted something that kind of matched the ethos of Partake, where you don’t feel like you’re sacrificing, you don’t feel like you’re being othered,” explains Woodard. “You get to fully participate and have something that’s delicious and looks as fun as the other options that are available for people without food allergies.” “The comments that we’ve gotten so far have been from various Girl Scouts who are so happy that they’ll be able to eat the cookie that they’re selling this year. It’s just been bringing tears to my eyes.” Up next for Partake is a line of breakfast foods, but Woodard isn’t going to stop there. On her entrepreneurial journey, she has learned a lot about how all kinds of groups are left out not just from snack time, but dinner tables and boardrooms, too, and she has tried to make belonging the thread that runs through the company as a whole. “We have a big focus on fighting food insecurity and have donated over a million meals to food insecure families. Our board is 80% women of color. We have a very diverse team,” she explains. And, their nonprofit Black Futures in Food & Beverage Fellowship is aimed at increasing diversity in the industry. “The [company’s] ethos really is coming to life in this dream partnership with the Girl Scouts, but it’s also, ‘How do we build a big enough table that people from all different walks of life, places, etc. feel welcomed and celebrated?’” It’s a lot to put on her plate, but Woodard has already shown she knows how to take on a really big project — one bite at a time.

articles.title: Welsh Gender Service cancelled 60 surgeries this year - minister
articles.summary: It is the first time figures have been given for numbers of surgeries cancelled by the service.
articles.body:
About 60 surgeries via the Welsh Gender Service (WGS) were cancelled for this year after NHS officials paused referrals in August, Wales' health minister has revealed.

It is the first time figures have been given for the number of people affected by the decision to pause referrals over concerns that patients who identify as transgender had been "appropriately assessed".

In a Senedd debate, Welsh Green leader Anthony Slaughter said patients were facing "unbearable limbo". Reform's Cristiana Emsley said it would be unacceptable to continue when "serious concerns exist".

Health Minister Mabon ap Gwynfor said he wanted "to bring certainty" as quickly as possible.

The body that took the decision, the NHS Wales Joint Commissioning Committee (NWJCC), has commissioned a review that is examining the referrals to see if any of the cancelled surgeries can proceed before the end of the year.

BBC Wales revealed in August that some patients found out about the cancellations while they were in hospital.

Earlier this month, the NWJCC said in some cases patients did not meet "the basic requirements for surgery".

Having an unsuitable body mass index (BMI) - a value derived from an adult's height and weight - was a factor.

It also said the proportion of Welsh patients progressing from referral for some types of surgery was "significantly lower" than across the border, while the rate of surgery referrals was "significantly higher".

The WGS provides referrals for adult patients living in Wales, but all NHS surgeries are carried out in England.

The surgery includes both masculinising and feminising procedures. They are not reversible.

Ap Gwynfor said the NWJCC had appointed a clinical review panel, and it was expected its work would commence "imminently".

"This review will prioritise those individuals who are further along the pathway to allow appropriate referrals to proceed as soon as possible," he said.

"The JCC has identified that approximately 60 patients were due surgery between the pausing of surgery in August and the end of December.

"Our priority is to bring certainty to these people as quickly as possible and the JCC are confident that all 60 of these cases can be reviewed before the end of December."

A wider independent review into the service is also taking place, with findings expected later this year.

Ap Gwynfor added: "I have met with the JCC and been clear that the urgent clinical review needs to be swift to minimise the disruption and distress for individuals on the waiting list.

"I have also been clear that I expect all patients impacted by this pause to have access to the necessary support whilst the review is undertaken."

Wales Greens leader Slaughter led the debate and told Members of the Senedd (MSs) that an "unbearable limbo" was being faced by patients.

He said some of whom had been left feeling "abandoned, alone and confused, having had the rug pulled from under them".

"They had jumped through every hoop asked of them, had arranged and rearranged their lives around this day," he said.

Slaughter urged ministers to review what he called "the failure of governance that led to both patients and the government being blindsided" and said "robust measures" should be put into place so that the JCC could be held to account.

Slaughter was supported by Plaid Cymru MS for Sir Fynwy Torfaen, Matthew Jones, who accused the committee of "not publicly or adequately" explaining its concerns.

But Conservative health spokesperson Natasha Asghar said: "The title of this short debate suggests that pausing sex change operations is unacceptable but that couldn't be further from the truth.

"There is nothing unacceptable about pausing irreversible surgery at the Welsh Gender Service while serious concerns are investigated."

Cristiana Emsley, Reform MS for Fflint Wrecsam, said she believed the halt was merited, saying: "Whatever our political differences, truth and patient safety must unite us.

"I accept that the pause might cause distress and patients must be supported, but what would be unacceptable is continuing irreversible referrals when serious concerns exist about referral appropriateness, clinical governance and patient safeguards".

The NWJCC said in an update on Wednesday that it would begin its review looking at patients whose surgery would be due to take place between August and December 2026.

"Reviews will start with those whose planned surgery dates were earliest and will continue in date order," it said.

"NWJCC has sought confirmation from the NHS England surgical providers that patients who are able to proceed with surgery will be prioritised."

It promised that this stage of the review would be completed by the end of December, and says "experienced gender clinicians" will undertake the work.

"Patients who are waiting for surgery in 2027, and those who are waiting for a surgical assessment, will also have their referral reviewed to confirm that the requirements for surgery have been met."

The NWJCC said it had not identified any patients who had come to harm, but said concerns were raised through "complaints, correspondence and other information".

articles.summary: Latvian President Edgars Rinkēvičs says Iran's drone tech helped Russia wage war in Ukraine as Latvia prepares to join a Strait of Hormuz coalition.
articles.body: UNITED NATIONS — Latvian President Edgars Rinkēvičs warned Wednesday that military cooperation between Russia and Iran poses a growing security concern, telling Fox News Digital in an on-camera interview that Iranian drone technology has helped Moscow wage war in Ukraine as Latvia prepares to contribute to a U.S.-led effort in the Strait of Hormuz. Speaking on the sidelines of the U.N. General Assembly, Rinkēvičs said Latvia, a country of approximately 1.84 million and still a core member of NATO's eastern flank, has already made the political decision to send military specialists to support international operations in the Middle East in response to President Donald Trump's request for European assistance. "Yes, I am concerned. Actually, we have already seen Iran helping Russia a lot, especially at the very beginning of Russia's aggression against Ukraine," Rinkēvičs said when asked about the growing cooperation between Moscow and Tehran. PUTIN AND IRAN 'NEED EACH OTHER DESPERATELY,' EXPERT SAYS, AS RUSSIA VOICES SUPPORT FOR REGIME "The first drones Iranian made, or Iranian-designed drones, were used by Russia.
